summary: role="toolbar" container with a single tab stop: arrow keys move focus between buttons, toggles, and menus, even across groups and separators.
whenToUse: Controls for a map, canvas, or viewer.
Compact actions above a table or document.
whenNotToUse: Navigating between pages: use NavigationMenu or Tabs.
Two or three independent buttons: ButtonGroup or Inline is enough.
Text fields: arrow keys move the caret and conflict with toolbar navigation.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Axis for arrow-key navigation and layout.

props.name: variant
props.description: With or without border and background.

props.name: ToolbarSeparator
props.description: Divider oriented perpendicular to the toolbar.

inherits: Props of react-aria-components Toolbar (className, style, data-*, events).

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the previous/next control; follows the reading direction in RTL.

accessibility: APG Toolbar pattern implemented by react-aria-components.
Separators have role="separator" and the correct aria-orientation.
Disabled controls are skipped by arrow keys.
responsive: The toolbar wraps onto multiple rows in narrow viewports; with many actions, move the less frequently used ones into a DropdownMenu.
customization: Use IconButton and Toggle variant="ghost" for a compact look.
commonMistakes: Using ToggleGroup selectionMode="multiple" inside the toolbar: prefer ToolbarGroup with controlled Toggles (see the Editor example).
Adding a TextField: arrow keys would be captured by the toolbar.
Using icon-only buttons without a label (label / aria-label).
limits: Inside a Toolbar, a multiple-selection ToggleGroup in react-aria-components 1.22 renders role="group" with aria-orientation (a disallowed attribute, flagged by axe): use ToolbarGroup with independent Toggles. A single-selection ToggleGroup (radiogroup) is correct.
